title: Reports screen, print-ready report views, report CSVs
objective: On-demand reporting per spec FR-64/FR-65 / PRD 19: report-card grid, print-ready views (browser-print PDF per A-5) and CSV per standard report; no scheduling.

SLA/Turnaround report content per PRD 17 (incl. SLA breaches by stage, underwriting delay queue)
implementation_details: Features/Reports/ReportCatalog.cs: registry {key, name, description, icon, permission, audience} — internal-tenant-overview and tenant-configuration permission-bound (Internal / tenant admin); GET /reports returns the caller-visible catalog

Report queries reuse dashboard query handlers where content overlaps (executive-weekly wraps GetExecutiveOverviewQuery etc.); new queries: SlaTurnaroundReportQuery (metrics per PRD 17.1, SLA breaches by stage bar data, underwriting delay queue rows), PipelineAgingReportQuery (open items by age/stage/owner/premium), EscalationQueueReportQuery (reuses alerts queue), TenantConfigurationReportQuery (reference lists + business rules snapshot), InternalTenantOverviewQuery (tenant status, active users, lead/quote volumes — cross-tenant, Internal permission)

Record the comparison result in this task's history.

e2e: reports.spec.ts: reports grid shows permitted cards only; Open report renders print-ready view with tenant/period/currency header; CSV button downloads; no scheduling UI present

findings.description: Cross-tenant isolation VERIFIED (no leak). internal-tenant-overview is the only report reading across tenants (ReportStore.BuildInternalTenantOverviewAsync uses IgnoreQueryFilters on UserTenants/Leads/ReferenceItems/Quotes). It is reachable only via ReportContentComposer.ComposeInternalOverviewAsync, which both GetReportViewQueryHandler and GetReportCsvQueryHandler invoke ONLY after ReportAuthorizer.AuthorizeAsync confirms the descriptor's binding permission (global.cross_tenant_reporting). Every other report stays tenant-scoped (explicit TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId predicate + active EF query filters). InternalTenantOverviewRow field order (LeadCount, QuoteCount, OpenLeadCount) matches the store's positional constructor call (leads.Total, quotes, leads.Open) — no field swap.

Per-key authorization (IDOR-class) VERIFIED. GET /reports/{key} and /reports/{key}/csv do NOT trust the catalog listing — both independently call ReportAuthorizer.AuthorizeAsync, which returns 403 (ReportForbidden) when the caller lacks the report's binding permission, so a user cannot fetch by key a report the catalog would hide. The internal CSV is additionally double-gated: GetReportCsvQueryHandler requires global.cross_tenant_export (FR-65) AND ExportService.AuthorizeAsync enforces the cross-tenant-context export gate. InternalTenantOverview_WithoutInternalPermission_ShouldReturn403 proves denial through the shared authorizer.

FLAG 1 (per-report permission bindings, PRD 19.1 prose) RULED ACCEPT / non-blocking. The concrete binding table is defensible and internally consistent: dashboard-backed reports inherit their dashboards.view_* permission (you cannot obtain a report whose on-screen dashboard you cannot view), escalation-queue -> alerts.view, tenant-configuration -> tenants.manage_settings, internal-tenant-overview -> global.cross_tenant_reporting (+ global.cross_tenant_export for its CSV). Enforced consistently in ListReportsQuery (catalog filtering) and ReportAuthorizer (per-key). No seeded-role regression (SeedUsers grants CrossTenantReporting to the Internal persona; drift guard + all suites green).
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the binding table with the product owner if PRD 19.1 is later made explicit; no code change needed now.

findings.description: FLAG 2 (PRD 17.1 SLA metric set) RULED ACCEPT — sufficient for AC-059/V-059. SlaTurnaroundReportQueryHandler renders received->assignment, received->quote-prepared, prepared->sent, sent->decision, underwriting-time, and received->sent turnaround (the last delegated to MetricDefinitions.AverageTurnaroundDays per AC-080's single-home rule); breaches-by-stage reuse the T-024 tenant SLA thresholds (sla_assignment/underwriting/received_to_sent_days); underwriting delay queue; turnaround-by-product-line. Cover-type / RM-team turnaround breakdowns are correctly deferred to the RM Performance dashboard's turnaround bars per FR-60/AC-059 placement (AC-059 distributes SLA visibility across Pipeline, RM Performance, Brokers, the Alerts SLA tab, and this report). No required report metric is missing.
findings.evidence: SlaTurnaroundReportQueryHandler.cs:44-139; ReportEndpointsTests.cs:74-101 (received_to_assignment==2, underwriting breach==1, delay-queue contains breaching lead)

findings.description: FLAG 3 (CSV filter pass-through) RULED ACCEPT. The view and CSV endpoints bind the identical DashboardFilter query params (from/to/productLineId/brokerId/rmUserId/regionId/teamOrRmId/brokerTypeId); the CSV handler composes the same ReportContent through the one ReportContentComposer, echoes the filters into the FR-65 metadata header (ReportFilterDescription), and renders via the shared T-039 ExportService (inheriting the injection guard + the export audit row, auditEntityType 'report'). ReportCsv_ShouldIncludeHeaderMetadataAndRespectFilters proves the productLineId filter is applied (motor lead present, property lead absent) and the metadata header (Tenant/Currency/Last refreshed/Data period) is emitted with the {tenant}-pipeline-aging-yyyyMMdd.csv filename.

Non-blocking test-coverage observation. Direct per-key 403 denial is proven for the internal report VIEW endpoint only (InternalTenantOverview_WithoutInternalPermission_ShouldReturn403); there is no dedicated test asserting (a) GET /reports/internal-tenant-overview/csv returns 403 without cross_tenant_reporting/cross_tenant_export, nor (b) GET /reports/{dashboard-key} view returns 403 for a caller who lacks that dashboards.view_* (only catalog-hiding of loss-analysis is asserted). The authorization mechanism is shared and generic (ReportAuthorizer, used by both view and CSV handlers), so the behavior is covered by construction and all suites are green; adding the two explicit cases would harden regression protection. Not blocking.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a CSV 403 case for internal-tenant-overview and a view 403 case for a dashboard report the caller lacks, in a future iteration.

findings.description: E2E deferral (reports.spec.ts, describe.fixme) RULED ACCEPTABLE, matching the established dashboard-overview.spec/exports.spec precedent. The four specs have real, ready-to-run bodies covering V-063/V-059/V-064 (permitted-card grid + no scheduling/cadence UI, print-ready header metadata, SLA underwriting-delay-queue section, per-report CSV download filename) and are blocked only on the T-041 seed persona/data + live compose stack. V-059/V-063/V-064 behavior is already proven by the real-Testcontainers backend suite and the frontend component suites. Un-fixme once T-041 lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove describe.fixme after T-041 provides the reports persona + seed data.
